question: Can stable transitions inside the image propose more cuts when noisy opposing edges leave the count ceiling at eight?

exploratoryProposal.expandedLimit: max(current edge-supported limit, median supported interior count + 1), capped at 16
exploratoryProposal.axes: Either axis may propose expansion; lower counts and both phases remain eligible.
exploratoryProposal.selection: The 75% rule was chosen after inspecting these 57 profiles. This is development analysis, not held-out validation or a production policy.

qualifications: Interior transitions are not a mathematical lower bound on slit count: one curve can cross a scanline more than once. These measurements propose search, never constrain geometry or acceptance.

The earlier hand-chosen maximum-12 diagnostic reduced dense-checker native disagreement from 5.61% to 2.71% in about 10.15 seconds. No fitter ran in this evidence study, and editable validation of that earlier expanded-count output remains outstanding.

The two inspected development photos are reused for transpose, horizontal/vertical flips, colour inversion, seeded 2%-border noise and one ignored corner. Stable proposed limits do not establish stable fitted geometry.
The original 55 masks are supplied as their saved binary fields; the two selected photos use saved float probability fields. This is not an end-to-end photo benchmark.
